Step-1.  Translate the intact first exon  

ATG TTT CTC GCT GGT ACT TCT GTG GAT GAA …  
Met-Phe-Leu-Ala-Gly-Thr-Ser-Val-Asp-Glu-…

The open reading frame is continuous until the normal stop codon far downstream (…TGA).

Step-2.  Examine every mutant in the same reading frame

Mutant-1  
ATG TTC TAC …  
Only two sense substitutions (Phe→Phe and Leu→Tyr) and another silent change (Arg remains Arg).  
Protein remains full length ⇒ enzyme very likely still active.

Mutant-3  
ATG TTT TAC GCT GGT GTC ACT …  
Several missense changes but no frameshift or stop codon.  
Full-length protein still produced ⇒ activity probably retained.

Mutant-4  
ATG TTT TAC GCT ACT …  
A three-base in-frame deletion removes a single Gly residue.  
Protein is almost full length; such a small internal deletion is unlikely to abolish function completely.

Mutant-2  
ATG TTC TAA …  
The third codon has become TAA, an UAA stop codon.  
This creates a premature termination very close to the start of the ORF.  
Result: either a 2-amino-acid peptide or, more likely, nonsense-mediated mRNA decay.  
In either case no functional enzyme will be produced, so synthesis of the anti-nutritional compound should stop.

Therefore the mutation most likely to eliminate production of the compound is the nonsense mutation in Mutant-2.

Answer: D
